newsitem.title: FRANCE: UNHCR Ogata expects trouble on Zaire front.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR Ogata expects trouble on Zaire front.

text.p: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata said on Thursday she expected difficulties in moving humanitarian supplies across combat lines in Zaire to reach hundreds of thousands of starving refugees.

Asked if the arrival of a multinational peace force would allow supplies to reach Mugunga camp, home to 400,000 Hutu refugees, Ogata said: "To reach the camp, we will require military assistance because there is a confrontation line which will have to be crossed.
"To get humanitarian corridors going, it's very important that the multinational force assist us...and I think it will probably be difficult to cross that confrontation line," she told reporters.
Reports from the area spoke of mortar, anti-aircraft and machinegun fire on Thursday around the teeming Mugunga camp about 10 km (six miles) west of rebel-held Goma on Rwanda's border.

Ogata, in Paris for a conference about Bosnia, was however upbeat about the multinational force's mission in general, saying: "It will help us enormously because it will return international humanitarian organisations (to disaster areas), assist the delivery of humanitarian aid and try to help refugees return home."
She said a UNHCR assessment mission had crossed back into Zaire but had not had time to complete its findings.
"We don't known how many people have died. We know that there were several hundred dead in both Goma and Bukavu but we don't know any more."
Ogata said she hoped assistance would begin to reach refugees next week once the first elements of the multinational force reached the field.
She spoke after heavy fighting erupted around Goma as Tutsi rebels sought to consolidate gains over their Hutu foes ahead of the arrival of the multinational peace force.
Goma residents said they believed the rebels were trying to take on the Hutu fighters before the arrival of the Canadian-led force, with a powerful U.S. military contingent, in a few days.
